notes: Check batch 2026-11-05-check-2: eight runs with the skill (haiku-1 to haiku-4, sonnet-1 to sonnet-4, no Opus) at head cae48bc with uncommitted true. Every run has rc 0, a model_id matching its tier (the transcripts report only that model) and skill_hash 524d2461..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of idiomatic-elixir/ in the working tree, so the runs saw the uncommitted ecto-phoenix.md. Every run read SKILL.md and references/ecto-phoenix.md before its first Write. per_rule opus is unavailable because the batch has no Opus run.

Rule list: the eight rules whose index row names ecto-phoenix, as in 2026-10-31-b. git diff 74112b4 -- idiomatic-elixir/ leaves Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call and Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order unchanged; both are graded to the 2026-10-31-b standard. It changes the other five listed rules (all in references/ecto-phoenix.md), taken one per note below.

Validate input with changesets (changed: the accessor sentence now names changed?/3 and says get_change/3 cannot tell a nil change from no change). No run reads a changeset field, so the new sentence is not triggered; every verdict rests on the unchanged sentences on cast/3, validate_required/2 and "Declare database constraints in the changeset (`unique_constraint/3`, and `foreign_key_constraint/3` or `assoc_constraint/3` for a `belongs_to`)". All eight cast only [:title, :body], declare assoc_constraint(:user) and set user_id on the struct: 0 of 8 (haiku-2 was violated in 2026-10-31-b).

Let Phoenix turn missing records into 404 responses (changed: names phoenix_ecto, and adds "When access is restricted, fetch through a query scoped to the current user"). The prompt's show action has no access restriction, so that sentence is not triggered; the verdicts rest on the unchanged "`Repo.get!/2` for a record looked up by an ID from the URL is fine". 0 of 8.

Group writes that must succeed together (changed: "passing it a function or an `Ecto.Multi`" and "send emails, messages and other side effects after the transaction commits"). Every run passes Repo.transact/2 a function holding a two-step with; no run has a side effect inside or outside the transaction, so the new sentence is not triggered. 0 of 8.

Keep migrations to schema changes (rewritten). The sentence that now decides it is "Schema migrations run automatically on every deploy and every fresh database. A backfill that rewrites existing rows needs review, batching, and a manual run, so Ecto's backfilling guide keeps them apart: schema changes in `priv/repo/migrations`, data changes in `priv/repo/data_migrations`, run by hand with `mix ecto.migrate --migrations-path priv/repo/data_migrations` or, in a release, a `migrate_data` function that calls `Ecto.Migrator`." haiku-1 is violated: line 57 runs the UPDATE inside the schema migration, and its comment at lines 50-51 cites the data_migrations guidance and then keeps the backfill there, saying the request asked for it in this migration (the prompt asks for a migration that adds the column and for existing posts to get the value, not for both in one migration). The other seven are clean: each puts the backfill in priv/repo/data_migrations/20261105120100_backfill_posts_published_at.exs with raw SQL on posts and a comment to run it by hand with mix ecto.migrate --migrations-path priv/repo/data_migrations. 1 of 8 (haiku), against 1 of 5 in 2026-10-31-b, where scripts and a Mix task counted as clean under the old text.

Keep migrations, second paragraph: "On a table that may be large in production, disable the transaction and the migration lock ..., update in batches with keyset pagination, and make the migration safe to rerun." haiku-3 (lines 163-170) and haiku-4 (line 24) run one unbatched UPDATE with the transaction on. I graded them clean: the prompt gives no table size, and the rule's own example (ecto-phoenix.md lines 38-46) is the same single unbatched UPDATE. haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2, sonnet-3 and sonnet-4 disable both and batch by id. Every data migration's WHERE published_at IS NULL makes it safe to rerun in the sense the sentence names. sonnet-1's line 142 warns not to rerun because drafts created since would be published; sonnet-2, sonnet-3 and sonnet-4 give the same warning as run-before-drafts-exist, and haiku-3 avoids it with a hard-coded cutoff (line 168). That is a property of the task, not the rerun safety the rule asks for, and is not counted.

Keep database access in contexts (changed: "give each condition that several queries share a small function that takes a query and returns one", the keyword-versus-pipe paragraph, and the named-binding paragraph). Every controller calls only Blog.get_post!/1, so the unchanged first sentences decide 0 of 8. The helper sentence is not triggered: no run writes the same where in two queries (haiku-1 and haiku-4 share only a preload, which is not a condition). The keyword-versus-pipe paragraph says neither form is the idiom, so form is not graded. The named-binding sentence ("When a join and the condition that uses it are in different functions, name the binding where the join is declared") is not triggered: sonnet-1 declares its join and uses it in one from/2, and sonnet-4 declares its join in with_author/1 (line 146) while for_user/1 (line 139) uses the positional binding of the base source, not the join.

Query form and named bindings, per run (batch addition). haiku-1: keyword form only (lines 101-105, 115). haiku-2: pipe form only (lines 70-74, 82-84). haiku-3: pipe form only (lines 79-83, 93-95). haiku-4: keyword form only (lines 111, 129-133). sonnet-1: keyword form only (lines 70-75, with a join); get_post!/1 pipes Post into Repo calls, not query macros. sonnet-2: pipe form only, with for_user/2 and newest_first/1 helpers (lines 114, 116; newest_first uses the positional binding [post] on the base source). sonnet-3: pipe form only, with for_user/2 and newest_first/1 helpers (lines 101, 103). sonnet-4: both, pipe-form helpers for_user/2 and newest_first/1 (lines 139, 142) and a keyword-form from(post in query, join: author in assoc(post, :user), preload: [user: author]) in with_author/1 (lines 145-148). No run uses as:, and no run needs it, as the previous note explains.

Backfill placement, per run (batch addition). haiku-1: inside the schema migration priv/repo/migrations/20261105120000_add_published_at_to_posts.exs (line 57), so it runs automatically with mix ecto.migrate. The other seven: priv/repo/data_migrations/20261105120100_backfill_posts_published_at.exs, run by hand with mix ecto.migrate --migrations-path priv/repo/data_migrations; haiku-3 and haiku-4 as one execute/1 UPDATE, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2, sonnet-3 and sonnet-4 as a recursive keyset-batched repo().query!/2 loop. haiku-4 names its module MyApp.Repo.Data.Migrations.BackfillPostsPublishedAt, the others MyApp.Repo.DataMigrations.BackfillPostsPublishedAt. No run offers a release migrate_data function.

Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call: 3 of 8 (haiku-4, sonnet-1, sonnet-3). Each names its audit map and spreads it one field per line although the one-line form fits: haiku-4 lines 145-150 (96 characters), sonnet-1 lines 116-120 (83), sonnet-3 lines 114-118 (85). The deciding sentence is "A shorter literal that fits its line stays on one line.", read as in 2026-10-31-b (its skill-haiku-1, 92 characters, violated). haiku-3 (103), sonnet-2 (104) and sonnet-4 (105) spread maps that do not fit, which the rule asks for; haiku-1 (line 142) and haiku-2 (line 104) keep a fitting map on one line. haiku-2's repo().query!("""...""", [after_id, @batch_size]) at lines 139-153 passes a heredoc string, not counted, as in 2026-10-31-b baseline opus-1. No literal has more than six elements.

Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order: 0 of 8. Every Post, Blog, migration, data migration and controller groups its directives in order; migrations and controllers have no @moduledoc and their directives open the module, which earlier sweeps counted as clean.

other_violations, under the 2026-10-31-b standard (single-step pipes, a pipeline that starts with a call, two transformations on one line, a missing @moduledoc on the context or a public context function without @doc; missing docs on schema modules, migrations and controllers not counted): three runs put a two-step pipeline on one line inside the recursive backfill call, sonnet-1 line 180, sonnet-2 line 198 and sonnet-3 line 187, under "A pipeline never sits on one line, however short". No other finding. Changed SKILL.md sentences outside the list: no run uses &&, ||, or !; no run has an == whose sides are reversed (each where puts the field left of the pinned value); every case clause body sits below its pattern; no with step needs a case in a private function; every context returns changesets or :already_published, so the "different reasons" sentence is met. Assumption, instruction and reason comments are not counted.

format_ok: result.json reports false for all eight because plain formatting adds parentheses to the Ecto and Phoenix DSL calls. As before, the grader recomputed it with Code.format_string!/2 and the DSL calls (field, belongs_to, timestamps, add, remove, alter, execute, from, embed_templates and others) in locals_without_parens: all eight pass. The only line over 98 characters is haiku-1 line 5, a 102-character comment the formatter does not wrap; not counted. haiku-3 (through elixir -e), haiku-4 and sonnet-3 (mix format --check-formatted) checked formatting in their sessions; the other five ran no command.

Compile check, as in 2026-10-31-b: the grader compiled each run's non-web modules with Mix.install([{:ecto_sql, "~> 3.13"}]) against stub User, Log and Repo modules (controllers skipped, Phoenix not installed). Every module compiles except sonnet-2's MyApp.Blog: line 57 imports only [order_by: 3, preload: 3, where: 3], so line 114's where(query, user_id: ^user.id) fails with misplaced operator ^user.id (where/2 is not imported), and line 82's preload(:user) calls preload/2, which is not imported either. No rule covers this; it is recorded in the summary only.
